title: Community Leader Patrick Katsuva Shot Dead in Beni, Steps From Security Positions
detail: Patrick Katsuva, president of the SOCICO civil society structure in Beni's Mambango neighborhood and head of a community child-protection network, was shot dead around 10pm on the night of Aug 25-26, less than 400 meters from a police squadron position and about 500 meters from a military post — raising local alarm over armed-group infiltration deep inside a security perimeter. Accounts differ on motive: a local official said he was shot while trying to stop armed men entering the neighborhood, while civil society figures say it may have been a targeted killing tied to his activism against insecurity and land seizures. No group has claimed responsibility. Spontaneous protests broke out in Mambango before calm returned by the afternoon of Aug 26.

media.caption: Map of the Beni area, North Kivu, where community leader Patrick Katsuva was shot dead in the Mambango neighborhood, Aug 25-26, 2026

confidenceReason: The killing itself is confirmed by local civil society and two independent North Kivu outlets; the perpetrators' identity and motive remain unconfirmed and no group has claimed responsibility.

title: DRC Grants Mota-Engil 30-Year Concession for Lobito Corridor Copper Railway
detail: President Félix Tshisekedi and visiting Angolan President João Lourenço presided over the signing in Kinshasa of a 30-year concession granting Portugal's Mota-Engil the rehabilitation, modernization and operation of the roughly 1,000km Dilolo-Sakania railway, which links DRC's Lualaba and Haut-Katanga copperbelt mining hubs to Angola's Atlantic port of Lobito via the Congolese section of the US-backed Lobito Corridor. Total investment over the concession period is expected to reach $1.8 billion, potentially backed by up to $1 billion in financing from the US International Development Finance Corporation; authorities project the upgraded line could eventually handle up to 13.7 million tonnes of freight annually. The deal is one of the largest concrete outcomes to date of the Trump administration's minerals-for-investment push in the DRC, running on a parallel track to the Washington Accords security framework.

confidenceReason: Deal terms and the signing are reported consistently by two Tier-2 outlets citing DRC and Angolan officials; exact concession valuation varies slightly across outlets ($1.25B-$1.8B depending on what is counted).
